title: Potawatomi fire-keepers and the Ohio Valley wars
summary: The Potawatomi, “keepers of the fire,” had no towns in Kentucky but joined the Northwest alliance that fought American settlement along the Ohio.
bodyMarkdown:
The Potawatomi (Bodéwadmi, "keepers of the fire") are an Anishinaabe people of the western Great Lakes, part of the Council of Three Fires with the Ojibwe and Odawa. Their towns stood around Green Bay, the St. Joseph River, Chicago and Milwaukee, and later in northern Indiana and Illinois. None was in Kentucky.

Their Kentucky tie is membership in the Northwest alliance of nations that fought American settlement north and south of the Ohio from the 1780s until 1794.

In June 1791 Kentucky volunteers under Brig. Gen. Charles Scott struck Wea and Kickapoo towns on the Wabash. Scott's report names no Potawatomi town. The Potawatomi signed the Treaty of Greenville in 1795.
Source: [The Potawatomi (Illinois State Museum, Midewin exhibit)](https://museum.state.il.us/exhibits/midewin/potowatomi.html)
Source: [Scott's Wabash Expedition, 1791: Scott's report (Project Gutenberg)](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/64829/64829-h/64829-h.htm)
